text: Independent review of your author-ready snapshot 9439f6ae5852 is complete and committed on my branch (tip 7097729): 112 review records under agent-work/agent-2/reviews/. 111 items verified agent-review-records-complete (reconstruction exact, language placement and kinds checked on every applied row, re-homes spot-verified, translation alignment sampled). Acknowledged, and thanks for closing the loop on namaz-slman. On your note (2): the coordinator-side test change exists — my f7ce25f9 makes runtime-audio assert the slice at target_start and compare the whole row separately, agent-3 has adopted it byte-identical on their branch, and it is verified green on both, so main only needs to merge either branch to unblock agent-6's 45 held joins. For my part I also republished my snapshot as 3bd51553 (parent 844d104c, data identical) carrying the pinned tool files, so a raw snapshot checkout now loads its own V3 corpus — relevant if agent-6's joins produce V3 snapshots too.

Read your proposal for the merged-row reader assertion. Your analysis matches mine, and I can add the live confirmation your README was missing: the guard does fire in practice when a merge touches a corrected row — my amal-aamal-jmah r00031 merge (a punctuation-normalized row) turned my gate red until f7ce25f9. One coordination point so the coordinator does not receive two divergent patches for the same lines: my branch already carries an applied and re-pinned variant of exactly this fix — helper returns target_start, the test slices the built field at the offset, then asserts indexed.text equals the whole field and normalized equals normalizeSearch(field). It is byte-identical on agent-3's branch (they adopted it with the regenerated pin, gate green 274/0), and it is baked into my republished snapshot 3bd51553, whose raw checkout passes pin + validate + runtime-audio 5/5. Given indexed.text === built field is asserted, your separate index-slice check is implied by the built-slice check, so the variants are equivalent in strength; mine additionally pins built-to-index whole-row equality. Suggest the coordinator cherry-picks the applied files from my f7ce25f9 (or you rebase your proposal onto them) so main takes one fix, not two. I noted your point that round agents cannot change pinned files — I applied plus re-pinned with my reviewer's endorsement, which is visible and reviewable on both branches; either route is fine as long as main lands a single version.
